headline: Netherlands Highly Skilled Migrant Visa 2026: Salary Thresholds and Process
metaDescription: Netherlands highly skilled migrant visa 2026: €5,942/month threshold for 30+, recognized sponsor rule, €423 IND fee, partner work rights and the EU Blue Card alternative.

sections.content:
The Netherlands highly skilled migrant scheme, known as the kennismigrant visa, is the country's main route for international professionals. For 2026 the gross monthly salary thresholds, excluding the 8 percent holiday allowance, are 5,942 euros for applicants aged 30 and over and 4,357 euros for those under 30.

A reduced rate of 3,122 euros applies to recent graduates and orientation-year holders. These thresholds are hard floors – being even one euro short means automatic rejection, with no discretion. Always confirm the indexed figures for your exact application year before signing a contract.
sections.title: 2026 salary thresholds: the hard floors

sections.content:
A critical feature of the scheme is that only an employer recognized by the IND as a sponsor – an erkend referent – can apply, and the employer files the application through the IND Business Portal rather than the employee. There is no labour market test and no separate work permit; the residence permit itself authorizes the work.

The IND application fee is 423 euros, paid by the employer. The statutory decision period is 90 days, though complete applications are typically decided in about two weeks. The permit matches the employment contract length, up to 5 years, and is renewable with a clear pathway to permanent residency.
sections.title: Recognized sponsors, fees and validity

sections.content:
Partners of highly skilled migrants receive a residence permit with full, unrestricted work rights, and family reunification is available – a notably generous setup compared with many countries. Graduates of top-200-ranked universities can also use the one-year search year permit to job-hunt in the Netherlands without a work permit.

The 30 percent ruling offers a partial tax-free salary benefit for up to 5 years for qualifying migrants, significantly boosting net pay. If you lose your job, you get 3 months to find a new recognized sponsor, or 6 months after holding the permit for 2 years under the rules updated from May 2026.
sections.title: Family rights, the 30% ruling and job loss protection

sections.content:
The main alternative is the EU Blue Card, with a 2026 threshold of 5,942 euros or 4,754 euros for recent graduates. It requires a university degree of at least three years and a contract of 6 to 12 months, offers EU-wide mobility after 18 months, and is valid for up to 4 years.

Which route fits depends on your profile: the kennismigrant scheme is simpler and has the under-30 and graduate discounts, while the Blue Card adds EU mobility for those planning to move between member states. Compare both against your contract terms before the employer files.
